quiz.title: THE SHRI RAM PYP4 Mathematics MHLE - 12: Data Handling
quiz.subject: maths

concepts.definition: A graph that uses bars to show and compare data.
A diagram with overlapping circles used to show similarities and differences between sets.
The numbers on the axis that show the units of measurement.
Lines used to record and count data quickly.
The number of times something occurs.

tasks.title: Task 1: This bar graph shows the favourite sport of grade 4 learners. Use the data represented in the bar graph to answer the questions.

questions.question: The scale on Y-axis is ____.
questions.hint: Look at the numbers on the Y-axis. They increase by 2 each time (0, 2, 4, 6, ...).
questions.solution: The Y-axis shows numbers 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. The difference between each number is 2, so the scale is 2.

questions.question: The sum of votes for football and tennis is equal to the sum of votes for ____ and ____ sports.
questions.hint: First, find the votes for football and tennis. Then, find two other sports whose votes add up to the same total.
questions.solution: From the bar graph: Football = 16 votes, Tennis = 8 votes. Sum = 16 + 8 = 24. Hockey = 12 votes, Rugby = 12 votes. Sum = 12 + 12 = 24. So, football + tennis = hockey + rugby.

questions.question: Imagine the number of votes for rugby doubles. Using the given scale, what will be its new height? Will it reach closer to the football bar or the hockey bar? Justify your answer.
questions.answer: New height: 12 units. It will reach the same height as the hockey bar.
questions.hint: Rugby currently has 6 votes. Doubling means multiplying by 2. Each unit on the Y-axis represents 2 votes.
questions.solution: Rugby has 6 votes. Doubling: 6 × 2 = 12 votes. Each unit on the Y-axis is 2 votes, so 12 votes = 6 units high. Hockey is also 12 votes (6 units), so rugby will match hockey’s height.

tasks.title: Task 2: Imagine you are planning a healthy meal and need to choose between adding almonds or spinach to your plate. Both foods are packed with important nutrients as Almond: Contains Protein, Healthy Fats, Vitamin E, Magnesium, and Fibre. Spinach: Contains iron, vitamin K, vitamin A, calcium, and fibre. Using the information, complete the following Venn diagram to compare the nutrients in Almonds and Spinach.

questions.question: Complete the Venn diagram to show which nutrients are unique to almonds, unique to spinach, and common to both.
questions.answer: Almonds only: Protein, Healthy Fats, Vitamin E, Magnesium. Spinach only: Iron, Vitamin K, Vitamin A, Calcium. Both: Fibre.
questions.hint: List the nutrients for almonds and spinach. Find which ones appear in both lists.
questions.solution: Almonds: Protein, Healthy Fats, Vitamin E, Magnesium, Fibre. Spinach: Iron, Vitamin K, Vitamin A, Calcium, Fibre. Fibre is common to both. The rest are unique to each food.

tasks.title: Task: Organizing and representing Data. Thando did a survey at her school. She asked her friends in class about their favourite chips flavour and recorded their answers: Chutney, Cheese, Chutney, Salt and Vinegar, Cheese, Chilli, Spring Onion, Cheese, Spring Onion, Chutney, Spring Onion, Cheese, Spring Onion, Salt and Vinegar, Chilli, Salt and Vinegar, Cheese, Spring Onion, Spring Onion.

questions.question: Organize the data in a table with columns: Favourite flavour of chips, Tally marks, Frequency.
questions.answer: Table should show: Cheese (5), Spring Onion (6), Chutney (3), Salt and Vinegar (3), Chilli (2).
questions.hint: Count how many times each flavour appears. Use tally marks to record each count.
questions.solution: Count each flavour: Cheese appears 5 times, Spring Onion 6 times, Chutney 3 times, Salt and Vinegar 3 times, Chilli 2 times. Record tally marks and total frequency.

questions.question: Draw a bar graph in your graph book to represent the data.
questions.answer: Bar graph with flavours on X-axis and frequency on Y-axis. Heights: Cheese=5, Spring Onion=6, Chutney=3, Salt and Vinegar=3, Chilli=2.
questions.hint: Label the X-axis with flavours and the Y-axis with numbers 0 to 6. Draw bars to match the frequency of each flavour.
questions.solution: Create a bar graph with flavours on the X-axis. The Y-axis should have a scale (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Draw bars for each flavour to match their frequency counts.

tasks.title: Enrichment Task: Choose any two times tables. Write the first 15 multiples of each. Then, use a Venn diagram to sort them: put the multiples of the first number in the left circle, the multiples of the second number in the right circle, and the common multiples in the middle.

questions.question: Choose any two times tables (e.g., 3 and 4). Write the first 15 multiples of each.
questions.hint: Multiply the number by 1, 2, 3, ..., 15 to find the first 15 multiples.

questions.question: Complete the Venn diagram to show the multiples of each number and their common multiples.
questions.hint: Find numbers that appear in both lists. These are common multiples.
questions.solution: Compare the two lists. Numbers like 12, 24, 36 appear in both, so they go in the middle of the Venn diagram.
